messages:
Marco: quick ask — can someone run a quick smoke + profiling run for cetus-6b v1? want p50/p95, tokens/s, mem footprint, and a prefix-cache hit check. also include a short tracing dump if anything spikes. target prompts: 512 and 2048 seq len.

Evan: grabbing this now. will run with int4 quant, kv-cache ON, batch_size=8. will post raw numbers and a small perf snippet.

BenchBot: job queued: bench-run-3419922222 (cetus6b:v1). estimated runtime ~12m. logs: /bench/logs/3419922222

Evan: results (smoke + micro-profiling):
- cmd: `./run_bench --model cetus6b:v1 --quant int4 --batch 8 --kv on --seq 512,2048 --trace short`
- seq=512: p50=41ms, p95=108ms, throughput=1.9k tokens/s, mem=6.4GB, cache_hit=72%
- seq=2048: p50=210ms, p95=640ms, throughput=870 tokens/s, mem=11.8GB, cache_hit=54%
- noticed sporadic latency spikes ~1.2s at ~30s into run; trace shows a large cudaMemcpy at kernel boundary (attach snippet).

Evan: attaching short trace excerpt:
```
[trace] 00:30.12 kernel_select: 0.18ms
[trace] 00:30.30 cudaMemcpy: 1204.6ms  <-- spike
[trace] 00:30.31 kernel_exec: 0.22ms
```

Priya: thanks. did you get any OOMs for 2048? and what was reserved GPU memory vs. used?

Evan: no OOMs. reserved ~12.7GB, peak used 11.8GB. fragmentation looked ~8% from the allocator logs.

Sasha: curious — what quant backend was used? nv_quant or custom packer? nvperf sometimes shows big memcpy when quant->dequant path hits.

Evan: used our new int4-packer (pack_v2). suspect dequant step before some fused kernels triggers memcpy. will re-run with nv_quant to compare.

Luis: I can run a tiling/kv-skip sweep — trying batch 4/8/12 and kv disabled/enabled to isolate hit pattern. should I use the same prompts?

Marco: yes please. include a run with batch 1 (to get pure latency) and batch 16 (to stress throughput). mark any runs that exceed 800ms p95 for seq=2048.

BenchBot: auto-summary: 12 runs completed. best throughput at seq=512: 2.1k tokens/s (batch 16,int4). regression check vs baseline (cetus6b:v0.9): p95 increased by +18% at seq=2048 on v1.

Priya: the +18% p95 is concerning — can we separate causes: kernel scheduling vs memcpy vs allocator fragmentation? Evan/Luis can you split runs with: (A) nv_quant + kv on, (B) int4-packer + kv off, (C) int4-packer + kv on + batch1.

Evan: will run A and C. planning to attach perf counters (cudaMemset/cudaMemcpy counts) and kernel timelines.

Luis: running B now. early peek: disabling kv reduced cache_hit obviously but p95 for seq=2048 dropped from 640ms -> 530ms (so memcpy/kv interaction may be the issue).

Sasha: that points to a KV cache hot path causing larger memcpy ops during cache refill. maybe our prefix caching copies large KV tensors synchronously. we should consider async prefetch or chunked memcpy.

Priya: can we get a quick diff of scheduler changes between v0.9 and v1? maybe a small change in kernel ordering exposed this.

Evan: confirmed: one scheduler tweak (reduce eager fusion) landed in v1 — likely changed kernel layout and exposed a memcpy window. reverting that flag in a local build reduced spikes in my quick retest.

Marco: action items: Evan -> run nv_quant comparison and attach perf counters (due EOD). Luis -> finish tiling/kv sweep and post CSV of runs (due tomorrow morning). Sasha -> prototype async chunked memcpy plan and estimate complexity. Priya -> draft a short rollback playbook if revert needed for canary.

Evan: noted. posting nv_quant vs packer numbers soon.

BenchBot: reminder: create canary with traffic 5% when ready. /cc @Marco @Priya

Marco: thanks everyone. feel free to ping if you need extra GPU time — I can open a burst request for this weekend. :thumbsup:
